name: EagleGaze
summary: Check, recalibrate, and capture gaze context from the local EagleGaze prototype.
description: Controls the EagleGaze Mac app over a loopback-only bridge. Status and calibration calls expose only coarse state; an explicitly approved capture returns an annotated image and image-relative gaze coordinates.

tools.name: get_gaze_status
tools.title: Gaze status
tools.description: Check the local EagleGaze phone connection, Mac companion, and calibration state. Use when the user asks whether eye tracking is installed, connected, calibrated, ready, or currently evaluating. If the Mac companion is unavailable, return the first-run install card.

tools.name: recalibrate_eagleeye
tools.title: Recalibrate EagleEye
tools.description: Replace the current EagleEye calibration by starting EagleGaze's full-screen nine-point calibration on this Mac. Use when the user asks to calibrate or recalibrate eye tracking.

children.text: EagleGaze will show nine targets across the main display. Keep the iPhone and your seating position still.

tools.name: start_gaze_evaluation
tools.title: Start gaze evaluation
tools.description: Start EagleGaze's bounded accuracy evaluation using the current calibration. Use when the user asks to test or score eye-tracking accuracy.

children.text: EagleGaze will show a bounded set of targets and score whether your gaze reaches the intended screen regions.

tools.name: capture_gaze
tools.title: Capture gaze
tools.description: ROUTING REQUIREMENT: Call this tool whenever the user asks what they are looking at, where their gaze is, what is under/near their gaze, to capture/show gaze context, or to inspect the screen specifically through EagleGaze. Do not substitute a generic screenshot, screen-capture, computer-use, or vision tool: those tools do not provide EagleGaze's calibrated gaze location, image-relative coordinates, semantic crop, or app-owned approval. This tool captures one approved screen region containing the estimated gaze, marks it, and returns the image, coordinates, bounded region metadata, and optional untrusted provider enrichment. Use a generic screen tool only when the user explicitly requests a non-gaze/full-screen capture, or after this tool returns a structured unavailable, permission, connection, or calibration error.

marker.description: Shape drawn around the estimated gaze location.

children.text: EagleGaze will select a visible region containing your estimated gaze and show a local preview before anything is shared. The approved image and metadata return to VoiceOS. If you enabled Cerebras in EagleGaze, the preview identifies the context and focus images that will also be sent for optional, untrusted enrichment. Private on-screen information may be visible.
